scope: New-round (v7) replay of exact GB (gram_b_r2) formulas only: the six strengthened inputs GB_{C,s} (template formula plus the 126-clause M_s tail; all twelve direct templates are parent-qualified), regenerated in memory by the pinned parent binder and bound to GBBINDING d917203d...c673; kissat 4.0.4 -> named FIFO -> parent RAM collector, then the parent drat-trim fed the measured CNF and the in-memory proof. Results are exact-input proof facts; no n8 theorem, transfer or novelty claim.

items.name: unsat
items.label: gbs7-ctl-unsat
items.preregistered_observation: genuine tiny UNSAT: the complete acceptance predicate holds and the stream filter dropped exactly one duplicate-literal normalization line in the formula phase (clause 9 '1 1 2 0'), so the exact filter class matches the pinned checker's real output (proof-phase lines, e.g. from a kissat deletion of that original clause, are counted and recorded as observed)
items.purpose: transport/acceptance control on a synthetic 3-variable formula; not part of the replay

items.name: sat-checker
items.label: gbs7-ctl-sat-checker
items.preregistered_observation: satisfiable checker CNF: complete equal transport (D == R, equal digests, N == D, parse line 3 variables / 7 clauses) and drat-trim self-exit 1 with the exact singleton status ['s NOT VERIFIED'] and no fatal-class diagnostic: an equal digest does not make a proof correct
items.purpose: transport/acceptance control on a synthetic 3-variable formula; not part of the replay

items.name: short-cnf
items.label: gbs7-ctl-short-cnf
items.preregistered_observation: intentionally short CNF delivery: the checker writer delivers the bound bytes except the final LF (written == bound - 1, sha256 of exactly that prefix, no error) while drat-trim self-exits 0 with exactly ['s VERIFIED'], N == D and the bound parse counts; only the measured feed fails, so a native VERIFIED cannot substitute for incomplete delivery
items.purpose: transport/acceptance control on a synthetic 3-variable formula; not part of the replay

items.name: truncate
items.label: gbs7-ctl-truncate
items.preregistered_observation: truncated proof: the feeder writes the collected proof except its last 2 bytes without any delivery error (D == R - 2, digests differ) and drat-trim consumes it to EOF (one count line, N == D or D + 1 for an EOF at a literal start, drat-trim.c L986-988); its outcome must be VERIFIED/0 or NOT VERIFIED/1 (the latter may carry only 'c ERROR: no conflict', L874, when the withheld bytes held the empty clause); the predicate fails on byte/digest equality
items.purpose: transport/acceptance control on a synthetic 3-variable formula; not part of the replay

items.name: suffix
items.label: gbs7-ctl-suffix
items.preregistered_observation: suffix proof: after the collected proof the feeder writes the 5-byte binary deletion 'd 1 2 3 0' (D == R + 5, digests differ) and the checker's consumed count N == D shows it read the suffix; outcome VERIFIED/0 or NOT VERIFIED/1 without fatal diagnostic; the predicate fails on byte equality
items.purpose: transport/acceptance control on a synthetic 3-variable formula; not part of the replay

items.name: digest-alter
items.label: gbs7-ctl-digest-alter
items.preregistered_observation: altered transported digest: the feeder flips bit 0 of the first one-byte literal of the first 'a' line in transit (that literal negated): D == R and N == D, but the transported digest differs from the collected and independently recomputed digests; outcome VERIFIED/0 or NOT VERIFIED/1 without fatal diagnostic; the predicate fails on digest equality alone
items.purpose: transport/acceptance control on a synthetic 3-variable formula; not part of the replay

items.name: early-close
items.label: gbs7-ctl-early-close

allowed_diagnostics: c ERROR: did not find p cnf line in input file

items.preregistered_observation: early checker close: drat-trim reads the complete header-less CNF, prints exactly the one diagnostic 'c ERROR: did not find p cnf line in input file' and self-exits 0 with no status line and no proof byte count; the feeder's first write, held until the checker was reaped, gets EPIPE with 0 bytes fed and stops cleanly (descriptor closed once, buffer released); every thread finishes, every descriptor is settled and no child is left
items.purpose: transport/acceptance control on a synthetic 3-variable formula; not part of the replay

acceptance: PASS iff every conjunct holds: (1) the freshly regenerated formula equals the GBBINDING record (header, variables, clauses, bytes, sha256, every piece) and the PRE-EXEC copy, and is re-hashed after admission immediately before each native spawn; (2) BOTH measured CNF feeds (kissat pipe, drat-trim pipe) finished without write or close error with written == bound bytes and sha256 == bound sha256; (3) kissat self-exit 20 (normal exit, no driver SIGTERM) and its status lines (log with only CR removed, lines starting with 's') exactly ['s UNSATISFIABLE']; (4) drat-trim self-exit 0, status lines exactly ['s VERIFIED'], no 's NOT VERIFIED' or 's TIMEOUT', no fatal-class diagnostic (ERROR, MEMOUT, illegal literal, error opening, wrong binary prefix, failed to reallocate), no 'early EOF' or 'clauses less than expected' line, exactly one 'c parsing input formula' line with the bound variable and clause counts; (5) the collector saw the actual FIFO EOF without error and read R > 0 bytes, an independent sha256 of the RAM buffer equals the collector's, and the plain-mode feeder wrote D == R bytes whose sha256 equals the collected digest, without delivery or close error; (6) exactly one 'c finished parsing, read N bytes from proof file' line with N == D; (7) the drat-trim stream filter read the raw stream to EOF without read, log-write or close error and the filtered log on disk hashes to the bytes it kept (it drops only exact duplicate-literal normalization lines, counted; the full raw stream hash/count is recorded separately); (8) no safety stop, exception, spawn error, skipped stage or exceeded SIGTERM grace; no driver signal latched during the pipeline or at evaluation; no exclusion breach latched by the scanner or the in-flight guard; no lane-scanner failure and the scanner stopped; all five worker threads started and finished; no descriptor left and no close error; both children reaped; no helper survivor. Anything else is UNKNOWN with reasons; a driver signal latched during evaluation downgrades PASS to UNKNOWN. Qualification additionally needs the commit record receipts/<label>.commit.json with qualified true: the receipt is first synced (file + directory), then the decision is taken with SIGTERM/SIGINT blocked (verdict PASS, durable receipt, no latched or pending signal, the driver the only thread) and published durably and atomically (os.link of the synced .prepare record); the item qualifies only when the completion record bound to that commit is published with no signal through the whole publication, no cancellation veto exists and the run's durable summary shows no stop or signal; (F4''') it is admitted only once the parent release attestation of the producing run exists (RELEASE_RULE). A SAT report, a safety stop or any settlement failure stops the desk. No retries: a new attempt needs a new parent GO and a new attempt tag; old UNKNOWN receipts are retained.
gate: Before each launch (stage 1; stage 2 is not a new admission): a fresh lane scan (native solver/checker processes plus python processes whose cwd or argv lies in the lane or a review/moqls8-* desk, excluding this driver and its children; python counts as busy if its CPU use over a 2 s libproc window is >= 50%; lane RSS includes every such python) and a fresh statvfs: launch only if lane busy + 3 <= 4 (v6b: the one live native + this driver + one transient helper), lane RSS of all other lane processes + max(fresh measured driver RSS, reservation; unreadable refuses) <= 11 GiB (gb reservation = the 6 GiB pipeline cap; controls 512 MiB), free >= 12,200,000,000 + 80 MiB, no exclusion breach (no parent GA replay native or replay/launch driver: the parent GA driver must have exited; no other kissat; no other GB pipeline driver), no helper survivor; two consecutive passing checks 60 s apart; otherwise sleep 60 s and re-check, total gate wait bounded by 600 s (v6b). No native spawn at or after 2026-10-22 19:00:33 PDT, nor one whose remaining stage backstops do not fit the driver chunk (v6b). gb items additionally need the unchanged parent stability rule read from observer v3 (control/resource-observer-live-v3.jsonl; addenda v1 9aff1085... and v2 6ddac862...; old amendment 0bbf4fdf...ce87): complete JSON lines, event records (start/restart) ignored and never reconstructed, every sample tz-aware with an int free, strictly increasing timestamps, last sample 0 <= age <= 30 s with free >= 13.5e9 + 80 MiB, >= 25 samples spanning >= 290 s within the last 300 s, max peak-to-later drop <= max(300,000,000, (free_last - 13.5e9) // 12); a malformed complete line or a naive, non-monotone or stale sample refuses; the rule and a fresh statvfs are re-read at the launch decision. Immediately before EACH native spawn (kissat, drat-trim) the launch threshold free >= 12.2e9 + 80 MiB, the latched stop/exclusion/scanner state, the 19:00:33 cutoff, the 21:50 deadline and the chunk fit are checked again (stage 2 also lane busy + 3 <= 4 and the 11 GiB lane total from the newest reading). The run also needs the parent GO record (validate_go) and, for gb items, the seven qualified control receipts (receipt + commit) of this script sha256.
in_flight_stops: In flight, every 0.25 s: pipeline aggregate RSS (driver incl. CNF parts and the RAM proof + the live child, libproc; a live child unreadable twice in a row is a guard failure) and free space; a scanner thread publishes lane scans every >= 1 s (helpers under 8 s deadlines; any failed reading is latched). SIGTERM the live child if a lane reading failed, a failure is latched or the reading is older than 30 s, an exclusion breach appears (latched by the scanner itself; foreign GB natives are recognized by cwd/argv in a GB desk or GB evidence tree, by ppid 1 or by a GB-driver parent), lane busy (other lane natives + hot python) + 3 > 4, lane RSS (other lane + max(pipeline measured, reservation)) > 11 GiB, pipeline aggregate > the item's cap (6 GiB gb, 1 GiB controls), free < 12,000,000,000, a kissat-sink overflow (> 32 MiB) or failure (v6b), driver elapsed > 10620 s or the absolute chunk end (v6b), stage wall > limit + 120 s (kissat 3600 s, drat-trim 6240 s), the host clock reaches 2026-10-22 21:50:00 PDT, a spawn error, a helper survivor, any exception after the first descriptor, or the driver receives SIGTERM (also checked immediately before each spawn and at each completion break); then wait at most 120 s, never escalate; result UNKNOWN and the desk launches nothing more. Stage 2 is skipped (UNKNOWN) unless stage 1 ended with kissat self-exit 20, the exact status line, a clean collector EOF with R > 0, a complete measured solver feed, finished stage-1 threads, no latched stop and the launch cutoff not reached.
transport: CNF parts in driver memory -> anonymous pipes /dev/fd/N (writer threads, sha256/count of exactly the bytes written; stage 1 kissat, stage 2 drat-trim argv[1]); proof: kissat -> named FIFO fifo/<label>.kissat.fifo (read end and keepalive opened by the driver before the spawn; keepalive closed at the reap) -> collector thread (sha256/count, actual EOF, chunks in RAM) -> after the reap and an independent buffer digest -> feeder thread (sha256/count of the bytes written; chunks released once written) -> drat-trim stdin (-i); drat-trim stdout+stderr -> anonymous pipe -> filter thread (full raw stream sha256/bytes/lines; only exact duplicate-literal normalization lines dropped and counted) -> logs/<label>.drat.filtered.log. No CNF or proof regular file; FIFO nodes retained; each native tool has its own TMPDIR and cwd tmp/<label>/kissat/ and tmp/<label>/drat/.
sequencing: A PRE-EXEC holds only controls (control:NAME, run in the listed order) or exactly one gb item (gb:ID:aN). One native at a time. A gb PRE-EXEC is admitted only with the seven control receipts of this script sha256 with their preregistered verdicts and qualified commit records, re-validated at preexec, at the run start and at every identity check. A control whose commit is not qualified (verdict differs from its preregistration or a late signal) stops the run; after a SAT report, a safety stop, a spawn error, an exception, a driver SIGTERM, a scanner failure, an unfinished thread, an unsettled descriptor, an unreaped child, a helper survivor or the 2026-10-22 19:00:33 PDT cutoff nothing more is launched. A label whose receipt exists is never re-run (controls: validated and skipped; gb: refused - a new attempt tag and a new parent GO are required).
parent_go: run requires GO = a parent-written JSON record under the new-round run's review/ (NEW_REVIEW) outside this desk with exactly: status 'PARENT_GO', desk 'physics/evidence/six-lane-20261018-96h/moqls8/evidence/gb-staged-v7', script_sha256 = this script's sha256, pre_exec_sha256 = the PRE-EXEC's sha256, scope 'controls' (control PRE-EXEC) or 'science' (gb PRE-EXEC) and items = the PRE-EXEC item specs in order. Its sha256 is recorded and re-checked at every identity check.
parent_release: (F4''') No receipt is admitted from producer bytes alone. qualification_problems() (used by validate_controls() for every science PRE-EXEC and run, and by the read-only 'qualification' subcommand) also requires the parent end/release attestation of the producing run: the regular file <NEW_REVIEW>/moqls8-gb-staged-release-gbs7-run-<run_tag>.json directly under the new-round review/ outside this desk (this desk never writes there), a JSON object with exactly schema 'moqls8-gb-staged-parent-release/5', status 'PARENT_RELEASE', desk 'physics/evidence/six-lane-20261018-96h/moqls8/evidence/gb-staged-v7', scope 'controls' or 'science' (the item kind), script_sha256 = this script, pre_exec_sha256 = the receipt's PRE-EXEC, run_tag, run_summary_sha256 = runs/run-<run_tag>.json, receipts = {label: receipt sha256} listing the label, driver_exit_code 0 (the exit status the parent observed after the run fully returned), owned_children_after_exit [], stop_or_signal_observed null and raw_audit 'PASS'. The parent writes it only after observing the run's process exit status 0, no surviving owned child and no stop or signal, and after its raw audit of the records; a non-zero exit status is never released.
